work_experience.org_name: Te Kāhui Tātari Ture (Criminal Cases Review Commission)
work_experience.title: Chief Executive (Tumu Whakarae)
work_experience.description: Inaugural Chief Executive of the Criminal Cases Review Commission, an independent Crown entity established in 2020 to investigate and review suspected miscarriages of justice in criminal cases. Reappointed for a further three-year term to 31 October 2028.

work_experience.title: Board Director
work_experience.description: Director of Transpower, the state-owned enterprise responsible for electric power transmission across New Zealand. Reappointed from 1 June 2025 for another term. Brings governance experience, public sector expertise, and knowledge of the energy sector and Te Ao Maori.

work_experience.title: Board Member
work_experience.description: Appointed as Board member of Health New Zealand in July 2025 for a 3-year term as part of the re-established board.

work_experience.title: Chief Executive
work_experience.description: Served as CEO of Waikato-Tainui for almost seven years, leading the iwi organization focused on the social, cultural, environmental, and economic wellbeing of over 80,000 tribal members. Subsequently served as Chair of Te Whakakitenga o Waikato for almost seven years including during COVID.

work_experience.title: Regional Director
work_experience.description: Served as Regional Director at Waka Kotahi, gaining significant infrastructure knowledge.

work_experience.title: Director of Strategy and Infrastructure
work_experience.description: Ran the largest non-clinical team at Middlemore Hospital during the COVID period.

work_experience.org_name: Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet (DPMC)
work_experience.title: Strategic Advisor, Policy Advisory Group
work_experience.description: Served as a strategic advisor in the Policy Advisory Group, providing free and frank advice to three Prime Ministers: Jim Bolger, Jenny Shipley, and Helen Clark. Involved in major policy decisions including Treaty Settlements, Cave Creek tragedy, and establishment of Maori Television Service.

work_experience.title: Policy Analyst / Manager
work_experience.description: Worked at the State Services Commission gaining understanding of the wider machinery of government.

work_experience.title: Policy Analyst
work_experience.description: First Wellington-based role after leaving the Waikato. Contributed to landmark policy on valuing unpaid domestic work alongside Dame Marilyn Waring.

work_experience.org_name: Ministry of Maori Affairs (Te Puni Kokiri)
work_experience.title: Policy Analyst
work_experience.description: Worked in the then-Ministry of Maori Development on Maori policy.

work_experience.title: Co-founder / Consultant
work_experience.description: Co-founded a consultancy company with her ex-husband focused on supporting the creative potential of Maori people, assets and knowledge, including Matauranga Maori (indigenous knowledge).

biography_summary: 帕雷卡维亚·麦克林（Parekawhia McLean）是新西兰著名的毛利裔公共部门领袖和公司治理专家，隶属于怀卡托（Waikato）部落的Ngati Mahanga氏族和Ngati Maniapoto部落。她于1965年出生于汉密尔顿（Hamilton），在怀卡托地区的Whatawhata乡村农场长大，有七个兄弟姐妹。她在Whatawhata小学和汉密尔顿弗雷泽高中（Fraser High School）接受教育，1987年获怀卡托大学社会科学学士学位，1991年获同校社会科学硕士学位（社会学专业），后赴美国威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校攻读公共行政与发展政策硕士学位。麦克林的公共部门职业生涯始于惠灵顿，先后在妇女事务部、毛利事务部和总理荣誉部长道格·基德（Doug Kidd）办公室担任私人秘书。她在公务员委员会工作后进入总理与内阁部（DPMC）政策咨询组，为三位总理——吉姆·博尔格（Jim Bolger）、珍妮·希普利（Jenny Shipley）和海伦·克拉克（Helen Clark）——提供战略政策建议，参与了《怀唐伊条约》和解、Cave Creek灾难和毛利电视台建立等重大政策决策。2010年，她回到怀卡托担任怀卡托-塔伊努伊部落（Waikato-Tainui）行政总裁近七年，随后在Waka Kotahi（新西兰交通局）担任区域总监、在马努考县卫生局（Counties Manukau DHB）担任战略与基础设施总监。2020年10月，她被任命为新西兰刑事案件审查委员会（Te Kahui Tatari Ture / CCRC）首任行政总裁，领导这个独立皇家实体调查和审查刑事案件中可能的司法误判，并于2025年10月获连任至2028年。在治理层面，她目前担任新西兰输电公司（Transpower）董事会董事（2020年任命，2025年6月连任）、新西兰卫生局（Health NZ）董事会成员（2025年7月任命，任期三年）、怀卡托大学校董会成员（代表毛利女王Te Arikinui Nga wai hono i te po）、体育怀卡托（Sport Waikato）董事，以及怀卡托-塔伊努伊部落实行委员会Te Arataura成员。她曾担任怀卡托-塔伊努伊部落治理机构Te Whakakitenga o Waikato主席近七年。2014年获怀卡托大学杰出校友奖。麦克林是两个女儿的母亲，现居怀卡托。

collection_meta.notes: Parekawhia McLean (Ngati Mahanga, Waikato, Ngati Maniapoto), born 1965 in Hamilton. Inaugural CEO of CCRC since Oct 2020, reappointed to Oct 2028. Transpower director since 2020, reappointed Jun 2025. Health NZ board member since Jul 2025. Previously CEO Waikato-Tainui (2010-2016), Regional Director Waka Kotahi, Director of Strategy at Counties Manukau DHB, strategic advisor at DPMC for 3 PMs. University of Waikato B.Soc.Sc (1987), M.Soc.Sc (1991), MA from University of Wisconsin. 2014 Distinguished Alumni Award. Extensive governance career across energy, health, iwi, sport, and justice sectors.
